item.title: Exploring the Local Location of Ollama Models on WSL2
item.author: hari@dasarpai.com (Dr. Hari Thapliyaal)
item.description:
Exploring the Location of Ollama Models on Local Machine
#

Ollama stores each model as files in a folder. On the Linux service in this article, that folder was /usr/share/ollama/.ollama/models. A copy you install for your own user often uses the home folder instead.

Linux and WSL, your user: ~/.ollama/models
Linux service on this machine: /usr/share/ollama/.ollama/models
Windows: C:\Users\<username>\.ollama\models

~ is your home directory. On this WSL machine that is /home/hari.

Question: What is Ollama? Is it like Docker?
#

Ollama is a platform designed to make running and interacting with large language models (LLMs) easier. It abstracts away the complexities of managing LLM models, GPU resources, and related configurations by offering a simple CLI interface. With Ollama, you can run, manage, and deploy LLMs locally or in various cloud environments without having to worry about the intricate details of setting up environments, downloading models, or configuring them.

item.title: ML Model Respository from Pinto0309
item.author: hari@dasarpai.com (Dr. Hari Thapliyaal)
item.description:
ML Model Repository from Pinto0309
#

What the PINTO model zoo holds
#

Katsuya Hyodo’s PINTO_model_zoo on GitHub is a free catalog of pre-trained vision and audio models converted for edge deployment. Each model lives in its own numbered folder; you pick a task, open the folder, and download the weights in the format your runtime needs (often ONNX).

Piece What you get
Repository layout One folder per model (192_open-closed-eye-0001, 059_yolov5, …) with README, sample scripts, and export subfolders
Model families Classification, 2D/3D detection, face and hand detection, pose, depth, segmentation, OCR, action recognition, GANs, transformers, and more — indexed below in 19 sections
File formats ONNX, TensorFlow Lite, OpenVINO IR, CoreML, FP32/FP16/INT8, plus optional TPU and TF-TRT builds (see the format key under Supported Formats)
Typical download Weight files (for example model_float32.onnx or quantized variants), sometimes labels or demo Python — not a full training pipeline
Run locally Copy the ONNX (or TFLite) file into OpenCV DNN, ONNX Runtime, or your edge stack; the repo’s per-model README lists input size and preprocessing
